questions.text: CHW Digital & Clinical Training: Training for Community Health Workers: (1) App usage training (data entry, sync); (2) Clinical protocol training (integrated Community Case Management - iCCM); (3) Danger sign recognition; (4) Patient counseling skills; (5) Refresher frequency; (6) Assessment of competence (exams/observation).
questions.evidence_required: Training curriculum, Attendance logs, Competence assessment scores
questions.africa_specific_notes: CHWs have varying literacy. Training must be hands-on. iCCM is the standard protocol.

questions.text: Telemedicine Provider Training: Training for doctors/nurses: (1) Webside manner (camera, lighting, empathy); (2) Remote physical exam techniques; (3) Limitations of telemedicine (when to refer); (4) Documentation standards; (5) Technology troubleshooting; (6) Legal/ethical guidelines.
questions.evidence_required: Telemedicine training modules, Provider certification, QA feedback loops
questions.africa_specific_notes: Doctors often resist telemedicine. Specific training needed on 'when to say no' and refer.

questions.text: Pharmacist/Dispenser Training: Training for e-pharmacy staff: (1) Order verification; (2) Drug interaction checking; (3) Patient counseling (via phone/chat); (4) Cold chain management; (5) Digital system usage.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Dispensers often have lower qualifications than pharmacists. Supervision and training critical.

questions.text: Patient App Usability & Literacy: Usability for low-literacy patients: (1) Icon-based navigation; (2) Voice/Audio instructions (local languages); (3) Video content; (4) Minimal text; (5) Accessibility features (large text); (6) User testing with target demographic.
questions.evidence_required: UX research reports, Accessibility audit, User testing videos
questions.africa_specific_notes: Text-heavy apps fail. 'Oral' users need voice/video. Icons must be culturally relevant.

questions.text: Health Literacy Support: Helping patients understand advice: (1) Plain language explanations (no jargon); (2) Teach-back method support; (3) Visual aids (diagrams of how to take meds); (4) SMS reminders/tips; (5) FAQ accessibility.
questions.evidence_required: Content readability analysis, Patient feedback, Educational materials
questions.africa_specific_notes: Patients often nod but don't understand. Visuals (sun/moon for dosage) work best.

questions.text: Digital Onboarding Support: Helping patients get online: (1) Agent-assisted onboarding; (2) Data bundle provision (zero-rating?); (3) Device setup assistance; (4) Password management support; (5) Family member onboarding (proxy).
questions.africa_specific_notes: First-time internet users need hand-holding. Agents often do the setup.

questions.text: Clinical Support Desk: Support for medical issues: (1) Access to senior clinician for CHWs/Juniors; (2) 24/7 availability; (3) Response time for clinical queries; (4) Escalation protocols for emergencies; (5) Case discussion forums.
questions.evidence_required: Support desk logs, Escalation protocols, SLA data
questions.africa_specific_notes: CHWs are alone in the field. They need a 'lifeline' to a doctor for complex cases.

questions.text: Technical Support for Health Workers: IT support: (1) Device replacement/repair; (2) App troubleshooting; (3) Data sync support; (4) Password resets; (5) Connectivity troubleshooting.
questions.africa_specific_notes: If the tablet breaks, the CHW stops working. Rapid replacement needed.

questions.text: Local Medical Capacity Building: Strengthening the system: (1) CME (Continuing Medical Education) credits; (2) Knowledge sharing (webinars, case studies); (3) Mentorship programs; (4) Partnership with medical schools; (5) Research capacity building.
questions.evidence_required: CME accreditation, Training calendar, Mentorship logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Tech should upskill the workforce, not just extract value. CME credits attract doctors.

questions.text: Supply Chain Capacity: Improving logistics skills: (1) Inventory management training; (2) Cold chain management training; (3) Forecasting skills; (4) Driver training (safety, security).
questions.africa_specific_notes: Supply chain is often the weak link. Training drivers/store managers is high impact.

scoring_notes: Layer 4 (Competence) for Healthcare in SSA: CHW competence is the foundation of primary care. Patient literacy requires non-text interfaces. Clinical support structures must exist to back up frontline workers.
